description: Carry subscriber traffic from about 1,420 ONTs through the OLTs and edge router to the leased middle-mile circuit; assign addresses (DHCP, RADIUS); serve DNS; deliver the 6 dedicated circuits
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Every subscriber and the office lose service; the 6 dedicated circuits allow about 43 minutes of downtime a month before credits (99.9%); a middle-mile loss of 30 minutes or more can meet the 667 OC3-minute NORS threshold (47 CFR 4.9(f)(2)); configurations change rarely, so nightly backups are enough
manual_workaround: None for subscribers. Field Technicians swap spare OLT line cards and optics from the warehouse; the network engineering consultant rebuilds router configuration remotely or on site
dependent_third_parties: Middle-mile and transit provider; OLT and router vendors (support and replacement parts); network engineering consultant; propane supplier
dependent_people_or_facilities: Network Operations Lead; 2 Field Technicians; network hut (power, batteries, generator)

description: Interconnected VoIP for about 440 numbers: calls placed through the hosted voice platform over the fiber; 911 calls routed by the platform to the county 911 center with the registered location
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers cannot reach 911 from their home or business lines; business customers lose their main numbers; voice depends on both BP-01 and the platform; number and feature settings change only on orders, so daily is enough
manual_workaround: Customers use mobile phones for 911 (script for representatives and the website banner); the platform portal can forward business numbers to mobile phones from any internet connection, including a technician phone hotspot
dependent_third_parties: Hosted voice platform provider (and its 911 routing network); middle-mile provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: Network Operations Lead; Customer Service Representatives (call forwarding requests)

business_process: Network monitoring, repair, and outage response
description: Detect device and circuit failures; dispatch technicians; run the outage procedure, including outage reports to the FCC and calls to the county 911 center when thresholds are met
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Unseen outages grow; NORS notification clocks run from discovery (120 minutes wireline, 240 minutes VoIP when a 911 facility is affected; 47 CFR 4.9(f), (g)); 911 outage contacts must be notified within 30 minutes when the 4.5(e) test is met (4.9(h)); DIRS reports are due daily when the FCC activates it (4.18)
manual_workaround: Customer calls and the answering service become the alarm; technicians check the hut and cabinets by hand; paper outage log
dependent_third_parties: Monitoring service vendor; answering service; network engineering consultant
dependent_people_or_facilities: Network Operations Lead; Field Technicians on call

description: Answer calls and counter visits; explain bills; take orders and payments; release account information after authentication; portal and AI assistant self-service after hours
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers can wait a day for routine questions; outage calls spike during network events; CPNI may be released only after the authentication in 47 CFR 64.2010, so a workaround must not relax it
manual_workaround: Answering service takes messages; representatives call back; no account details are released without the BSS (no paper customer list)
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-06; SYS-07; SYS-08; SYS-02 (office phone lines); SYS-10
dependent_third_parties: BSS vendor; hosted voice platform provider; answering service; MSP
dependent_people_or_facilities: 2 Customer Service Representatives; Office Manager; office building

description: Build new service orders, activate ONTs in the EMS, set speed profiles in RADIUS, port and assign telephone numbers on the platform
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: New installs can be rescheduled; about 15 installs a month; activation data is rebuilt from the BSS order if lost
manual_workaround: Reschedule installs; activate from the OLT command line with the network engineering consultant if the EMS is down
dependent_third_parties: Hosted voice platform provider; BSS vendor; OLT vendor

description: Monthly bill run on the 1st; import toll call charges from the platform CDR export; post payments from the processor; collections
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $92,000 billed a month; a bill run can slip a few days; the cash reserve covers about 45 days; payments continue through the processor hosted page
manual_workaround: Delay the bill run; take payments by phone through the processor virtual terminal
dependent_third_parties: BSS vendor; payment processor; hosted voice platform provider

business_process: Lawful intercept and law enforcement requests
description: Receive court orders and other lawful process; verify authority; arrange voice intercepts through the platform and broadband intercepts through the CALEA trusted third party; keep the required records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Orders are rare (one since 2017) but must be carried out promptly with the carrier's affirmative intervention (47 CFR 1.20000; 1.20003); records must be complete and secure (1.20004)
manual_workaround: The General Manager reaches the TTP and the platform provider by phone; paper records in the locked cabinet
dependent_third_parties: CALEA trusted third party; hosted voice platform provider; telecom regulatory consultant
dependent_people_or_facilities: Owner and General Manager; Network Operations Lead (technical contact); network hut

business_process: Office administration, payroll, and regulatory filings
description: Shared-drive documents; HR files; payroll through an outside payroll service; FCC filings prepared by the regulatory consultant (CPNI certification by March 1)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs biweekly; filing deadlines are known weeks ahead
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll service; the consultant keeps copies of past filings
dependent_third_parties: Productivity suite vendor; backup service (MSP); payroll service; telecom regulatory consultant
